searches.note: Twenty one searches of a share of twenty eight, none the author's. Five were restricted to a producer's domain (bedellcellars.com, lenzwine.com, wolffer.com twice, macariwines.com) and read as primary for the house's own facts. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.

What a search contradicted was set right with its source; what rested on no source was cut; every glass note, untested in the author's draft, was rewritten from tasting notes found; a source whose address names a living critic was met and is not cited.

tested: Founding 1980 and the sale: the house's Heritage page gives 1980 and 1999; Wine Spectator and Dan's Papers give April 2000, with an investment of 1999 in one; both years now taught.
Musée's first vintage 2005 and Chuck Close's label: Dan's Papers; the daguerreotype of the picked grapes found in no source and cut.
Grapes: the house's listings of 2005 (Merlot led, with Cabernet Sauvignon and Petit Verdot) and 2014, two listings of 2010 (with a little Syrah), the 2019 store page; reworded.
The 2009 Merlot at the luncheon of January 2013: Dan's Papers, Riverhead News Review, the house; kept, the first claim hedged as the house's.
Glass: Tastings.com for 2019, VinePair and the Wine Folly guide for 2015; rewritten.
Michael Lynne (1941 to 2019): Wine Spectator, dead at 77 in March 2019; Chuck Close (1940 to 2021) kept.
changed: story: was sold in 1999 to Michael Lynne; now 1999 by the house's account and 2000 by the press, to a group he led, since Wine Spectator and Dan's Papers date the purchase to April 2000.

story, table and card: was a daguerreotype of the very grapes picked for the first Musée; now the label of the first Musée, the 2005, made by Chuck Close, which Dan's Papers confirms; the daguerreotype of those grapes was found in no source read.

wine.grapes: was later vintages giving Petit Verdot and Malbec more; now Merlot leads most vintages, by the house's listings of 2005 and 2014 and two listings of 2010, with Cabernet Franc, Malbec or a little Syrah in some years.

wine.glass: was an untested note with a saline edge; now black cherry, plum, cedar, dried violet, lead pencil, liquorice and dried mushroom, medium body and chewy tannin, as tastings of 2010, 2015 and 2019 give them.
questions: the story stem now says around 2000 and its explanation gives both years; the wine explanation no longer names Malbec as a fixed part.
sources: Edible Manhattan and the store page give way to Dan's Papers and Tastings.com.
open: The claim that the 2009 Merlot was the first New York wine at an inauguration is the house's, told as such; one quotation of the owner says the first Long Island winery.

tested: Planting 1978 at Peconic and the change of hands in 1988: 27 East, Long Island Wine Country, the house; kept, buyers left unnamed as accounts differ.
Library: the house's page, held back after the 1993 vintage, Old Vines Merlot and Cabernet; story set to it.
Old Vines tier from the oldest blocks, made only in strong vintages, peak at fifteen to twenty years: the house's pages; kept.
Glass: Tastings.com 2010, the house's 2015 notes, a review the house quotes for 2002; rewritten.
Blind tastings: 1996 in one account, comparative tastings over the years in another; kept undated.
changed: story: was holding back from the early 1990s; now after 1993, a strong year for reds, part of the Old Vines Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon, by the house's library page.

wine.glass: was an untested note with dried fig; now black plum, dark cherry, raspberry, cedar, cigar box, leather, mocha and black tea, medium in body with smooth tannin, from Tastings.com, the house's notes of 2015 and a review the house quotes for 2002.
others: Estate Selection Merlot was for drinking sooner, untested; now told by the house's own comparison with the Old Vines.
sources: Dan's Papers gives way to Tastings.com for the glass.
open: Accounts differ on the buyers of 1988 (a couple in one, a partnership under a lease with an option to buy in another); the record says only new owners, which every source supports.
The blind tastings are told without date or result: one account dates the first to 1996.

tested: Founding 1983 at Aquebogue: Grape Collective, RiverheadLOCAL, the Wine Folly guide; kept.
The founders' roots: born in Lebanon (Grape Collective); a German family of vintners (RiverheadLOCAL); the Pfalz rests on a student blog and the hospitality on nothing: reworded.

The Chenin of 1989: an abandoned vineyard, pull-out list, spared at a neighbour's urging in one account; plantings of 2000, 2005 and the clone of 2012: northforker and Grape Collective; reworded as a story.
Screw caps: the first on Long Island in 2007 by local press; hedged.
Palmer founded 1983 and bought in 2018: Dan's Papers and the Palmer guide; Palmer lies in Riverhead, so not called a neighbour at Aquebogue.
Riesling and Cabernet Sauvignon among the estate's vines: a listing of its grapes; kept.
changed: story: was a winegrowing family of the Pfalz and a background of hospitality in Lebanon; now a German family of vintners and born in Lebanon, since the Pfalz rests on a student blog only and the hospitality on nothing found.

story, sites, card and question: was a neighbouring vineyard they ran out of time to clear; now an abandoned vineyard whose Chenin was spared, told as a story, since accounts differ on why the vines survived.
story and making: was an early taker of screw caps; now the first on Long Island, in 2007, by the local press, hedged.
story and trap: Palmer was its neighbour at Aquebogue; now nearby, since Palmer's address is Riverhead.
wine.sites: the new clone of 2012 is cut from the site line, left in the story only through the dates 2000 and 2005, which two accounts give.
others: Riesling was the grape of the Pfalz where a founder grew up; now the estate's own Riesling, which a listing of its vines confirms.
sources: one of the two Palmer press items gives way to RiverheadLOCAL on the family's roots.
open: Paumanok's claim to be the first maker of Chenin Blanc in New York is the house's, told as such.

tested: Land 1978, Sagpond 1988, the winemaker 1992, first Sagpond rosé 1993, renaming and first Estate Rosé 1996: the house's timeline; VinePair and 27 East give 1997 for the renaming; the house's year taught.
The summer party story: not found; cut.
Christian's Cuvée from the oldest Merlot field, planted 1990: the house's Wine Stand page; kept.

Estate Rosé appellation Long Island: the house's product page; kept. Grapes: VinePair confirms Merlot, Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Gewürztraminer and Riesling in the house's rosé blends; kept.
Summer in a Bottle picked days later: not found; cut; its Côtes de Provence version from the house's sheets added.
Glass: the house's product note for 2025; rewritten.
The death on the last day of 2008: Decanter and 27 East; kept, the founder left undated.
changed: story: was the first rosé in the early 1990s after a summer party; now the first Sagpond rosé in 1993 and the first Estate Rosé in 1996, by the house's timeline; the party story was found in no source read and is cut.
story and table: was the summer wine of the South Fork, the wine that taught the Hamptons to drink rosé and made pale and dry the fashion; each ranked or overclaimed and is now told plainly.
wine.glass: was an untested note of strawberry, peach and grapefruit; now honeysuckle, violet, ripe fresh fruit and a creamy, yeasty note, the house's own note for 2025.

others, trap and card: was Summer in a Bottle picked several days later; the later picking was found in no source read and is cut; now its Côtes de Provence version, from the house's own sheets, and the year of the first Estate Rosé.
wine.label: Estate Rosé now dated to 1996 by the house's timeline.
open: The renaming is 1996 by the house's timeline and 1997 by 27 East and VinePair; the house's year is taught.
The making (picked in waves, extended lees contact) and the Merlot lead rest on the house's technical note, read through the author's search; VinePair confirms the grapes but not the shares.

tested: Founding 1995, father, son and daughter in law: the Wine Folly guide, the house; kept unnamed.
Biodynamic from the first plantings and home made compost: the house's family page; kept.
Land owned for over fifty years: the house and the Wine Folly guide; the 1960s cut.
Longhorn cattle: a press account of twenty five longhorns and a family interview saying the herd is now mixed; reworded.
Bergen Road the flagship, only in premium vintages, blends of 2010, 2015 and 2021: the house's pages, Forbes through search; kept.
Cutchogue tasting room: the house's page says it was relaunched under another name in 2022; cut.
Glass: the Wine Folly guide and VinePair; rewritten.
changed: story and card: was the land in the family since the 1960s; now about half a century before the vines, since the house and Wine Folly say over fifty years and the 1960s rests on one account.
story and card: was a herd of longhorn cattle; now a herd of cattle, longhorns at first, since a family interview says the herd is now mixed.
story and trap: the second tasting room at Cutchogue is cut, since the house's own page says that site was relaunched under another name in 2022: a fact true only for some years.
wine.glass: was an untested note with graphite; now damson plum, raspberry, blackberry, cedar and a hint of green pepper, medium bodied with fine grained tannin, by the Wine Folly guide and VinePair.
sources: Dan's Papers gives way to the Wine Folly guide's wine notes.
open: The origin of the name Bergen Road is not taught; the estate's address is Bergen Avenue.

livingNamesMet: Bedell: the founders Kip and Susan Bedell; the winemaker Richard Olsen-Harbich; the owner's widow; Senator Chuck Schumer, who chose the inaugural wine.
Lenz: the founders Peter and Patricia Lenz; the buyers of 1988 Peter and Deborah Carroll, and John Pancoast in one account.
Paumanok: the founders Charles and Ursula Massoud and their sons Kareem, Nabeel and Salim; Palmer's seller, a daughter of the founders Bob and Lorraine Palmer.
Wölffer: the founder's children Marc and Joey Wölffer and the winemaker Roman Roth.
Macari: Joseph Macari Jr., Alexandra Macari and Gabriella Macari; Joseph T. Macari Sr., life dates not found, not named.
Critics met in sources: Jancis Robinson and James Suckling; none is named in the fragment. The read-together agent may add the family names to people.json.
swaps: No swap proposed by the author; the refuter rules all five picks stand: each house's own page and the press name the flagship taught (Musée, Old Vines Merlot, Chenin Blanc, Estate Rosé, Bergen Road).
codexTension: The region summary gives The Hamptons, Long Island AVA as 1985, the North Fork 1986 and the island wide AVA 2001; the records agree. The region's producers line for Lenz says its Merlot and Chardonnay first put North Fork wines beside Bordeaux at blind tastings; no source read dates or tied those tastings to Bordeaux, so the record says only comparative blind tastings, and the line is reported, not edited. No library record exists for any of the five houses. No Codex record was edited.
